text:
Matty Beniers keeps showing up at the right moment. His overtime winner against Calgary on Nov. 4 was the third of his career, per Alison Lukan, and his wins-added total (70th of 515 skaters) says his goals have mattered more than most.

That is the good half. The other half is that Beniers, playing close to 19 minutes a night lately as Seattle's top center, has been on the ice for more chances against than for: 46% of attempts and 46% of expected goals at 5v5, about level with the team without him. His four goals on 17 shots is a 23.5% shooting rate, and the Kraken have scored six more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice.

Evolving-Hockey sounded the same warning about last season: his 1.9 wins above replacement ran well ahead of 0.7 expected. He has a real habit of drawing penalties, though, worth about two goals a season by their count.

The 2023 Calder winner is still 24. The thing to watch is volume: 17 shots in 16 games is low for a top-line center.
headline: Beniers is winning games without winning the shot share
